title: Decentralize CPU-GPU bridge and vectorized batch I/O to cut host-side latency and contention
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Production traces show recurrent host-side bottlenecks on the CPU->GPU pipeline during prefill and the start of decode. Symptoms: frequent short-lived memcpy spikes, threadpool wake/sleep churn, and serialized submission to GPU queues that inflate p50/p95 latency for short chats and high-concurrency embedding workloads. These issues are pronounced on multi-socket instances with NUMA domains and on pods sharing host CPU with other runtime components. Goal: reduce host overhead (copies, syscalls, lock contention) and reduce end-to-end latency variability by decentralizing the CPU-GPU bridge, moving to vectorized batch I/O, and implementing per-lane lock-free queues and NUMA-aware buffer allocation.
proposal: 1) Per-GPU bridge workers: replace a single host-side central submitter with per-GPU worker threads pinned to local cores/NUMA domains. Each worker manages a small set of submission lanes and maintains its own pinned buffer pool. 2) Vectorized batch I/O: coalesce multiple small prefill writes into vectorized gather/scatter operations using a small adaptive coalescer. 3) Lock-free ring lanes: implement multi-producer single-consumer lock-free ring buffers for fast enqueue from user threads into per-GPU lanes. 4) Pinned, reusable scatter-gather buffer pool: reduce allocation and page-fault cost by reusing pinned buffers and amortizing registration. 5) Adaptive prefill scheduler: token-aware, size-aware scheduler that batches short-prefill requests but keeps long-running prefill low-latency. 6) Kernel hint integration: provide kernel-selection hints (short-prefix vs long-seq) to the bridge so kernel selection reduces unnecessary KV cache prefetch when running short-prefill paths.
metrics_and_targets:
- Reduce host memcpy bytes per request by >=2x on average.
- Reduce CPU sys time for prefill path by >=30%.
- Reduce p95 latency for short chat requests (<=128 tokens) by >=20%.
- Reduce threadpool wake-ups per second on high-concurrency hosts by >=40%.
- No >5% regression in throughput for long-sequence batches.

progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Prototype per-GPU worker that accepts batches via a single MPSC ring reduced host memcpy sizes by ~2.1x in microbenchmarks.
2026-02-18: Implemented pinned buffer pool prototype. Observed 28% reduction in page-faults for high-concurrency prefill workloads on c5n-like hosts.
2026-02-24: Threadpool integration tests revealed starvation when lanes are imbalanced. Added backpressure and lane-stealing policy to avoid stalls.

2026-02-28: Initial end-to-end A/B running 5% traffic in staging. p95 for short chats improved by 18%, host sys CPU down 33%. Noted a rare stall related to kernel registration on older kernels; added detection and fallback.

2026-03-01: Design review complete. Feedback: add configurable coalescing thresholds, expose per-lane metrics, and ensure graceful fallback to current central submitter at runtime. Action items created.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Per-GPU worker bug causes stalls or starvation. Mitigation: implement watchdog that falls back to central submitter and instrument events for rapid rollback.
Risk: Kernel/Vendor differences for pinned buffer registration. Mitigation: detection layer that chooses between pinned pool and standard allocations per host type.
Risk: Additional complexity in scheduling could regress long-batch throughput. Mitigation: gated rollout with throughput regression checks and opt-out config per deployment.
Risk: Increased memory usage from pinned pools. Mitigation: LRU eviction, size caps per-NUMA domain, and memory-pressure eviction hooks.
Risk: Lock-free algorithms are tricky to maintain. Mitigation: encapsulate lane library with a simple stable API and pair with thorough fuzz and concurrency tests.
review_feedback: PM (E. Morales): prioritize short-chat tail latency improvements; keep coalescer conservative by default.
Runtime lead (S. Novak): require per-lane metrics before extending to production; add telemetry for enqueue/dequeue slow paths.
Security (L. Ito): confirm pinned buffer pool uses appropriate mlock limits and does not expose data between tenants; mark for infra security checklist.
